This is a pair-specific extension (single-representation description to cross-representation comparison/ordering), not mere shared wording or code proximity, so a same-rank forward direction is justified. Evidence is limited: both endpoints and their parent Content Standards carry unresolved ancestry with framework-root fallback (not used here as placement evidence), source evidence is truncated, and no Learning Components were supplied, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit in BASIC 4 (rank 0), Strand 1 Number, Sub-Strand 1 Counting, Representation & Cardinality, but under different Content Standards (B4.1.1.1 place value to 100,000 vs B4.1.1.4 interpreting negative and positive numbers). B4.1.1.1.6 is skip counting forwards/backwards in 50s and 100s up to/from 10000; B4.1.1.4.2 is counting forwards/backwards with positive and negative whole numbers through zero. Their LCs confirm a shared forwards/backwards counting-sequence skill applied to two distinct number domains (large multiples vs integers through zero). This is meaningful conceptual coherence in counting direction and sequence fluency, but neither statement's mastery is substantively required for or developmentally extended by the other, and equal grade rank offers no basis for direction; shared token/trigram overlap ('count', 'forwards', 'backwards') and the common code prefix alone are not developmental evidence.
